correctness.rationale: The normalized density and two CDF expansions are derived from exact gamma and Dirichlet integrals, with uniform bounded-simplex remainders. The signed first nonzero coefficient is a strictly positive scalar times \(R_n( eta)-1\). \(\log R_n\) has positive derivative at zero, strictly negative second derivative, and tends to minus infinity, giving one positive root. AM–GM distinguishes \(n=2\) from \(n\ge3\). Exact integer comparisons establish \(2<\kappa_3<21/10<\lambda_3\). Gamma-tail and all-summands-large bounds give matching upper-tail logarithmic rates, hence the opposed signs and crossings. The packaged standard-library checker passed 136 supporting assertions; finite numerics are not used to prove infinite quantifiers.

value.rationale: Sum and maximum are competing natural risk aggregation statistics, and the lower-tail-matched scaling comes directly from the recent literature. The unique \( eta\)-threshold quantifies which statistic has more near-zero mass for every finite dimension. The open three-summand interval establishes true stochastic incomparability rather than mere failure of distributional identity, making it a motivated qualitative phenomenon for tail-risk approximation.
